section_summary.extract_value: This section reports testing a hypothesized structural model in a single study (N = 249) controlling for BMI; model fit was good (e.g., original model CFI = .98, SRMR = .04, RMSEA = .05; revised model CFI = .99, SRMR = .04, RMSEA = .03). Several nonsignificant paths were removed to create a trimmed model, one modification (adding a path from attachment anxiety to order perfectionism) improved fit, and the final model accounted for substantial variance in body appreciation (40.5%), intuitive eating (44.4%), and other variables.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: "The number of participants (N = 249)..."; "The structural model in Fig. 1 provided a good fit to the data (CFI=.98, SRMR=.04, RMSEA = .05)..."; "The revised model (CFI=.99, SRMR=.04, RMSEA=.03), \chi^2 (27, N=249)=31.74, p=.242..."; and "a sizable percentage of variance (40.5%) in body appreciation... Body appreciation... predicted 44.4% of the variance in intuitive eating."

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports testing of a structural equation model using Mplus with N = 249 participants, controlling for BMI and evaluating model fit via CFI, SRMR, and RMSEA. The original model fit well and was trimmed by removing nonsignificant paths, with a revised final model (reported fit indices) explaining notable variance in body appreciation and intuitive eating; no separate studies (e.g., 'Study 1') or multiple sample subsets are mentioned.
